hook.text: Latin 'pater,' English 'father.' Latin 'tres,' English 'three.' The pattern is no coincidence.

buildup.text: Jacob Grimm (yes, the fairy tale one) discovered a systematic shift in consonants.

discovery.text: Proto-Indo-European p→f, t→θ, k→h in Germanic languages—a chain reaction of sound changes.

twist.text: Grimm's Law was one of the first proofs that language change follows regular, predictable rules.

climax.text: This discovery launched comparative linguistics as a science in the 19th century.

punchline.text: Fairy tales and phonetics—Grimm mastered both.

quiz.question: What did Grimm's Law describe?
options: Systematic consonant shifts in Germanic languages
